suggestions.assertion: Reports a quantified count of assertion-free test methods (expects 4, e.g. in ProductGridTests.java and InvoiceLookupTests.java)
suggestions.reason: This assertion would pass on a coincidentally-correct total count even when the named tests are wrong, since it only checks 'expects 4' without requiring the specific 4 tests to be named. The actual output here reached '4' by substituting two WIP tests (already covered by a separate finding) for two real omissions (ProductGridTests.testOpenProductGridAndFilter and InvoiceLookupTests.testInvoiceGridLoadsWithoutError). Consider requiring the assertion to check that the count is backed by the correct named test methods, not just a matching total.

suggestions.assertion: Reports a quantified empty-catch-block / swallowed-exception count backed by a grep
suggestions.reason: Good catch opportunity confirmed by the transcript itself: the executor ran the correct grep, got a number in the right ballpark (49, close to the manifest's 37), and then talked itself out of reporting it as a finding with reasoning that doesn't hold up on inspection (claiming it was 'already captured' elsewhere when it wasn't). This suggests the skill's guidance on when multiple findings can be consolidated may be under-specified or too easy to over-apply as an excuse to skip a mandatory grep-backed finding -- worth tightening the skill's instructions on this point.

No assertion checks for factual accuracy of individual sentence-level claims within a finding (e.g., the review misattributes testSortProductGridByPrice's behavior to include a discarded isDisplayed() call that actually belongs to a different test in the same sentence). This is a real, if minor, precision defect that all 18 assertions miss because they check presence/quantification of findings, not sentence-level correctness of the supporting narrative.

The locator-distribution assertion requires 'roughly matching the ~31%/31%/38% positional/id/css split' but the review used an entirely different taxonomy (locator syntax: id/css/xpath/name) rather than a fragility-based taxonomy (positional/stable-id/css-class), and never computed percentages at all. This is a clean, discriminating miss -- worth keeping as-is since it cleanly separates reviews that did the fragility-bucketing work from ones that only did a syntax tally.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong result overall (14/18, 78%) on a review that is extremely well-evidenced and file:line-accurate everywhere it was spot-checked (God Base Class, raw-type leakage, cross-file duplication, sleep count, WIP package, raw-Selenium layer leakage all matched the ground-truth manifest closely). The 4 failures are substantive, not nitpicks: a required quantified empty-catch finding is entirely absent despite the executor having run the correct grep and talked itself out of reporting it; the assertion-free-test count hits the right total by substituting wrong tests for right ones; the locator-distribution finding never produces the percentage breakdown the assertion calls for (different taxonomy entirely); and one heading breaks the 'every heading names a problem' rule by praising a correctly-wired build property. These are exactly the kind of findings a human reviewer comparing against the seeded-defect manifest would also flag, so the assertions are doing their job here.
